title: flagstaff plugin
description: A plugin is one plain object. Everything in it is data that can be read without running it; the only functions allowed are a component's `static` (required) and `frame` (optional). A spinner or component without a static projection is refused at register().

name.description: The plugin's name; also the prefix a host may use when two plugins contribute the same key.

contract.description: The plugin contract this object follows. A host refuses a newer contract than it knows.

tokens.description: A roundel theme: semantic token name to a hex colour, contrast-checked when flown.

propertyNames.description: roundel's ten semantic tokens, and nothing else — `roundel`'s own validate() refuses any other name.

glyphs.description: Symbols by meaning: `ok`, `fail`, `warn`, `info`, `running`. A plugin that ships glyphs changes every built-in that draws one.

spinners.description: Spinner styles by name, in cli-spinners' shape plus the static projection.

borders.description: Border styles a box can be drawn with, by name.

components.description: Components by name: `static(state)` returns the text a pipe, an agent or a screen reader gets; `frame(t, state)` is the optional animated form.

resolvers.description: bellpull resolvers by name: extra directories searched for an executable, before PATH (negative rank) or after it (positive). Two resolvers with one name shadow; two names both apply, in rank order.

widgets.description: caique prompt widgets by kind. The six built-in kinds — text, confirm, select, multiselect, password, path — cannot be replaced: a plugin adds kinds of its own.

handlers.description: closeout exit handlers. The phase decides the order they run in, not their position in this list.

sources.description: seniority configuration sources by name, ranked against the built-in layers: a flag is 0 and a declared default is 40, and a plugin source sits strictly between.

commands.description: burgee commands this plugin contributes. Each is read by exactly the code a program's own command is, and a burgee plugin must declare `contract`.

hooks.description: burgee lifecycle hooks. parse rewrites argv before a command is resolved; preRun opens around a command, and exactly one of postRun or onError closes; shutdown fires once as the program leaves, by any path.

enforce.description: burgee: order this plugin's hooks before (`pre`) or after (`post`) the others.

interval.description: Milliseconds between frames on a terminal.

static.description: What a pipe prints instead of the animation.
(state) => string. Required: the projection every non-terminal mode prints.

frame.description: (t, state) => string. Optional: the frame at t milliseconds since hoisting.

sample.description: Two states to *show* this component with: `flagstaff check` and the docs gallery render `running` then `done`. Omitted, they assume `{ phase: 'running' }` and `{ phase: 'done' }` and say so in the output. The loop never reads it — a running program's state comes from the program.

interval.description: Milliseconds between repaints when `frame` is given; 80 when omitted.

border.description: cli-boxes' shape exactly, so that corpus imports unchanged.

capability.description: One paratext capability: what it says to the terminal, when the terminal is believed to understand it, and what prints when it does not. No functions, so it travels through JSON. `encode` and `fallback` are templates: `{field}` is the field's value, `{field|base64}` is it base64-encoded, and `[ … ]` is emitted only when every field inside it has a value.

name.description: How callers name it. Registering an existing name replaces it — how a caller corrects a guess we got wrong.

osc.description: The OSC code this speaks, or 'BEL' for the bell and for protocols that are not OSC at all, such as Kitty's.

when.description: When the terminal is believed to understand it. Every clause must hold; `termProgram` and `envAny` are ORs within themselves. Guesses — no terminal answers 'do you do OSC 1337' — and therefore data a caller can replace.

tty.description: Refuse a pipe. Almost always true: a file that receives OSC gets control bytes in it.

termProgram.description: Any one of these TERM_PROGRAM values.

envAny.description: Any one of these environment variables merely being set, as VTE announces itself.

term.description: An exact TERM — Kitty is xterm-kitty.

encode.description: The bytes, as a template, for a terminal that does understand.

fallback.description: What to print when it does not — PRINCIPLES rule 6. '' is a legitimate answer, a window title having nothing to say in a log; absence is not, which is why this is required and may be ''.

capabilities.description: paratext capabilities by name — the OSC section of a plugin, read the way flagstaff reads `spinners`.

capabilityDocument.description: What paratext's `check()` accepts. Two shapes, and only one of them survives 1.0.

oneOf.description: The family shape: a plugin carrying its capabilities under `capabilities`.
Deprecated: one capability as the whole document, the shape paratext's schema had before this one absorbed it. Accepted for one minor release, removed at 1.0 — `check()` validates it and says so.

widthRange.description: One inclusive code-point range, as [low, high]. A single code point is written [n, n].

widthOverride.description: A linegauge width override: the column count a named set of code-point ranges occupies, for a terminal that disagrees with the Unicode tables. Data only — no function, so it can be written in a config file, diffed, and printed by `linegauge check` without running anyone code.

ranges.description: The code points this override applies to.

columns.description: Columns each cluster in those ranges occupies: 0 for a zero-width mark, 1 narrow, 2 wide.

why.description: The terminal or the reason. Required, because a width table with no provenance is one nobody can audit when it turns out to be wrong — which is the normal outcome for ambiguous width.

widths.description: linegauge width overrides by name — the measurement section of a plugin, read the way flagstaff reads `spinners`.

resolver.description: One bellpull resolver: where to look for an executable, and when.

rank.description: Search order against PATH: negative searches before it, positive after.

paths.description: Directories to search. `{VAR}` is substituted from the environment; each must be absolute, or start with a `{VAR}` that holds an absolute path.

extensions.description: Extensions to try on Windows, in place of PATHEXT.

when.description: When the resolver applies. Leave it out and it always does.

envAny.description: It applies when any of these environment variables is set.

widget.description: One caique widget: how a prompt kind of the plugin's own is drawn.

static.description: (spec) => string. Required: what a pipe, an agent or a screen reader gets instead of the interactive prompt.

frame.description: (t, spec) => string. Optional: the animated form; leave it out and the widget is line-mode only.

sample.description: Two named states of plain data that `caique check` renders the widget with.

name.description: How the handler is named in a report, including the one the deadline prints when it does not return.

phase.description: When it runs. Defaults to `release`; `restore` is closeout's own last phase and a plugin may not use it.

run.description: (info) => void | Promise<void>. Required: the cleanup itself.

source.description: One seniority source. Exactly one of `values` (static) or `read(runtime)` (fetched) gives its answer.

rank.description: Precedence, strictly between the flag (0) and the declared default (40): a source may not beat what the user typed, nor sink below the default.

location.description: The file, URL or variable set a person would go and look at.

option.description: One burgee option, keyed by its camelCase name; the flag is its kebab-case form.

dependsOn.description: Options that must be set with this one; each must be another option of the same command.

exclusive.description: Options that may not be set with this one; each must be another option of the same command.

deprecated.description: What replaces this option, e.g. '--force'. `true` alone, or an empty string, is refused: a deprecation names its replacement.

command.description: One burgee command node, declared exactly as a program's own command is.

path.description: The words a user types. May not repeat a path the program or an earlier plugin already declares.

effects.description: What running it does to the world. Required on any command that runs; `withheld` serves it to people and keeps it out of the MCP tool list.

deprecated.description: What replaces this command. `true` alone, or an empty string, is refused.

run.description: (ctx) => unknown. What the command does; its return value is the `--json` envelope's data.

load.description: () => Promise<module>. A lazy form of `run`, imported on dispatch.

filter.description: `{ command: RegExp }`: fire only for commands whose path matches.

handler.description: (ctx) => void | Promise<void>. Required. On parse it may return the string[] argv to use instead.
